subject: phy
title: DC Circuits
subtitle: Kirchhoff's laws, series and parallel circuits, potential dividers.
concept: Kirchhoff's first law (KCL): the sum of currents entering a junction equals the sum leaving — conservation of charge.
Kirchhoff's second law (KVL): the sum of EMFs around any closed loop equals the sum of p.d.s — conservation of energy.
A potential divider splits a supply voltage in proportion to the resistor values; it is the basis of sensor circuits.

notes.heading: Series and Parallel Circuits
items: Series: same current through all components. Total resistance = sum of individual resistances (Rₜ = R₁ + R₂ + ...). The supply voltage is shared — larger resistors have larger p.d.s.
Parallel: same p.d. across all branches. 1/Rₜ = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + ... Total resistance is always less than the smallest branch resistance. Current divides in inverse proportion to resistance.

notes.heading: Kirchhoff's Laws
items: KCL (junction rule): the sum of currents entering a junction equals the sum leaving. This is conservation of charge — charge cannot accumulate at a junction.

KVL (loop rule): the algebraic sum of all EMFs around any closed loop equals the algebraic sum of all potential drops (IR terms) around the same loop. This is conservation of energy — the energy supplied by sources equals the energy dissipated.

notes.heading: Potential Divider
items: Two resistors R₁ and R₂ in series across a supply voltage Vₛ. The output (p.d. across R₂): V_out = Vₛ × R₂ / (R₁ + R₂). The output is larger when R₂ is a larger fraction of the total.

Sensor circuits: replace R₂ with an LDR or thermistor. As temperature increases, the thermistor resistance falls → V_out falls (if thermistor is R₂). Connecting the output to a transistor switch allows automatic control.

notes.heading: Power in Circuits
items: Power dissipated in a resistor: P = IV = I²R = V²/R. In series: the resistor with the highest R dissipates the most power. In parallel: the resistor with the lowest R (highest current) dissipates the most power.

definitions.body: At any junction in a circuit, the total current entering equals the total current leaving; conservation of charge.
The sum of all EMFs in a closed loop equals the sum of all potential drops (IR): Σε = ΣIR; conservation of energy.
Two resistors in series used to split a supply voltage; output voltage ∝ fraction of total resistance across output component.

workedExamples.q: Calculate the output voltage of a potential divider: V_s = 9 V, R₁ = 4 kΩ, R₂ = 2 kΩ.
A 12 V battery (internal resistance 1 Ω) is connected to 5 Ω and 7 Ω in series. Find the p.d. across the 7 Ω resistor.

mistakes: Forgetting to include internal resistance in the total resistance.
Using V = ε (full EMF) across external components — the terminal p.d. is ε − Ir.
Adding resistors in parallel using R_total = R₁ + R₂ — this is the series formula.
tips: To find R_total for two parallel resistors: R = R₁R₂/(R₁+R₂) ('product over sum').
Potential divider: output is larger when the output resistor is larger relative to the other.
For sensor circuits with LDR: as light increases, R_LDR decreases → if R_LDR is R₂, V_out decreases.
